subject: physiology
title: Pancreatic Secretion, Bile Composition, and Enterohepatic Circulation

steps.tx: The exocrine pancreas secretes approximately one to two litres of clear, alkaline digestive fluid daily into the duodenum. Pancreatic juice contains two functionally distinct fractions: an aqueous fluid rich in bicarbonate secreted by ductal cells, and an **enzymatic pancreatic fraction** synthesized and stored as zymogen granules within acinar cells.
steps.say: Pancreatic juice provides an alkaline bicarbonate fluid from ductal cells and digestive zymogens from acinar cells.

left.title: Pancreatic Acinar Cells
points: Stimulated predominantly by cholecystokinin (CCK) and acetylcholine
Utilize IP3 and intracellular calcium signaling cascades
Synthesize trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, amylase, and lipase

right.title: Pancreatic Ductal Cells
points: Synthesize and secrete alkaline bicarbonate-rich fluid
Utilize cyclic AMP and apical CFTR chloride channels
Neutralizes acidic gastric chyme entering the duodenum

steps.tx: Bicarbonate secretion by pancreatic ductal epithelial cells is driven by apical anion exchange coupled to the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator. Mediated by cyclic AMP in response to duodenal secretin, active **ductal bicarbonate secretion** raises luminal pH to eight, optimizing catalytic activity for pancreatic lipases and proteases.
steps.say: Ductal cells secrete bicarbonate via CFTR and chloride exchangers, raising duodenal pH to eight to optimize digestion.

nodes.label: Duodenal Secretin Binds Basolateral GPCR on Pancreatic Ductal Cells
Adenylyl Cyclase Activation Elevates Intracellular cAMP and Activates PKA
Apical CFTR Channels Open, Conducting Chloride Ions into the Lumen
Apical Cl-/HCO3- Exchanger Extrudes Concentrated Bicarbonate in Exchange for Cl-

steps.tx: At low resting basal flow rates, pancreatic juice exhibits high chloride and low bicarbonate concentrations. As secretin stimulation accelerates flow rate, chloride concentration plummets while bicarbonate concentration climbs toward one hundred twenty milliequivalents per litre, establishing an inverse relationship between **pancreatic anions and flow rate**.
steps.say: At high secretin-stimulated flow rates, bicarbonate concentration climbs while chloride drops inversely.

steps.tx: Hepatic parenchymal cells synthesize primary bile acids (cholic acid and chenodeoxycholic acid) from cholesterol via rate-limiting cholesterol seven-alpha-hydroxylase. Conjugation with glycine or taurine produces amphipathic **conjugated bile salts**, which possess a low pKa that prevents passive precipitation in the acidic proximal duodenum.
steps.say: Hepatocytes synthesize bile acids from cholesterol, conjugating them with glycine or taurine to form amphipathic bile salts.

vis.alt: Bile acid synthesis and pancreatic enzyme secretion
vis.caption: Bile acid synthesis from cholesterol, conjugation pathways, and biliary lipid micelle formation.

steps.tx: Between meals, the sphincter of Oddi remains tonically contracted, diverting continuous hepatic bile flow into the gallbladder. The gallbladder mucosa actively reabsorbs sodium chloride and water, yielding an eight-fold **concentrated gallbladder bile** rich in bile salts, lecithin, cholesterol, and conjugated bilirubin.
steps.say: The gallbladder concentrates hepatic bile eight-fold by actively reabsorbing salt and water between meals.

left.title: Hepatic Canalicular Bile
points: Secreted continuously by hepatocytes and cholangiocytes
Low bile salt concentration (~30 to 50 mmol/L)

right.title: Gallbladder Concentrated Bile
points: Viscous, dark-green concentrated fluid (~85% to 90% water)
Active NaCl and water reabsorption concentrates solutes 5- to 10-fold
High bile acid concentration (~150 to 300 mmol/L)
Vulnerable to cholesterol super-saturation and gallstone precipitation

steps.tx: Entry of dietary fatty acids and amino acids into the duodenum stimulates I cells to release cholecystokinin. Cholecystokinin produces coordinated gallbladder evacuation by inducing forceful **gallbladder muscular contraction** while simultaneously triggering nitric oxide-mediated receptive relaxation of the sphincter of Oddi.
steps.say: Cholecystokinin contracts the gallbladder and relaxes the sphincter of Oddi, squirting concentrated bile into the duodenum.

nodes.label: Dietary Lipids and Peptides Enter Duodenum from Gastric Antrum
Duodenal and Jejunal I Cells Secrete Cholecystokinin (CCK) into Blood
CCK-A Receptors Contract Gallbladder Smooth Muscle via IP3/Ca2+
Vagally Mediated Nitric Oxide Relaxes Sphincter of Oddi; Bile Enters Duodenum

steps.tx: Following lipid digestion and micellar absorption in the upper jejunum, over ninety-five percent of secreted bile salts are actively reclaimed in the terminal ileum via the apical **sodium-dependent bile acid transporter**. Reabsorbed bile salts travel via the portal vein back to the liver for resecretion, completing enterohepatic recycling.
steps.say: Over ninety-five percent of bile salts are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum via ASBT, returning to the liver via portal blood.

nodes.label: Jejunum: Bile Salts Form Mixed Micelles to Facilitate Lipid Absorption
Terminal Ileum: Apical Sodium-Dependent Bile Acid Transporter (ASBT) Reabsorbs Salts
Portal Vein Transports Bound Bile Salts Directly Back to Hepatic Sinusoids
Hepatocytes Extract 95% of Salts via NTCP, Resecreting Them into Canaliculi

steps.tx: Surgical resection or extensive Crohn disease inflammation of the terminal ileum disrupts this efficient conservation cycle, spilling unabsorbed bile salts into the colon. Bacterial deconjugation in the caecum stimulates mucosal cyclic AMP and chloride secretion, producing debilitating **choleretic secretory diarrhea** and steatorrhea.
steps.say: Ileal resection spills unabsorbed bile salts into the colon, stimulating chloride secretion and causing choleretic diarrhea.

vis.alt: Bile acid malabsorption and secretory colonic diarrhea
vis.caption: Bile acid spillage into colon, mucosal secretomotor stimulation, and choleretic bile acid diarrhea.
